The activity log now shows everything BombVault does, the whole app got a deep code-and-UI audit, and the folder-set domain has a clearer name.

## Added

- **The Activity Log now shows everything.** Off-site replication, retention prunes, restore drills, tamper tests and the flash-ZIP export are recorded as first-class runs alongside backups, restores and updates - each with duration and outcome, filterable like everything else. What happens in BombVault is now visible in BombVault.
- **Weekly digest.** An optional once-a-week summary through your existing notification channels: how many runs succeeded or failed, how much was backed up, whether every off-site copy is current, and the week's failures - one message instead of a feed to check.
- **Update check visibility.** Containers with "update after backup" now show when the image was last checked and the outcome (up to date / updated / check failed), so "no news" and "never reached" are no longer the same thing.
- **Backup engine cache limit.** The persistent restic cache introduced in v6.7.0 now cleans up after itself and respects a configurable size limit (default 4 GB), evicting the least-recently-used repository cache first.

- **Private registry support (#106).** Post-backup image updates can now pull from private or sponsor-gated registries (GHCR, Docker Hub, lscr.io, custom hosts). Add your registry credentials under Settings → Storage → Container registries; BombVault picks the matching credential from the image reference automatically and stays anonymous everywhere else. Tokens are stored encrypted, are never echoed back by the API, and can be replaced or removed per registry.
- **Dates in the activity log (#104).** Every log line now carries a locale-aware date next to the time (e.g. "23.07. 05:04:08"), and the filter finds dates too - type an ISO date like 2026-07-23 or the short form shown in the log to see just that day.

- **Cron schedules (#107).** Every schedule (backups, off-site, drills, tamper tests, digest) can now use a raw 5-field cron expression - e.g. `0 */6 * * *` for every six hours. The schedule builder gets a "Cron" mode with live validation, a preview of the next three run times, and clickable examples. Existing preset schedules are untouched; switching to Cron prefills the equivalent expression.

## Changed

- **"Files" is now "Folders" ("Dateien" → "Ordner").** The domain backs up folder sets, so it is now named that way everywhere, in all 26 languages. Nothing changes technically - schedules, backups and settings carry over.
- **Retention pruning is batched.** Scheduled multi-item runs now prune once per domain after the loop instead of once per item - the same batching that v6.7.0 brought to off-site replication, applied to retention. Nightly runs get faster again; the batched prune appears in Run History like a manual one.
- **One hover style everywhere.** The customize pencil, heatmap pills and source toggles now fill on hover exactly like the app's tabs.

- **The append-only check is findable (#109).** It now sits as "Append-only check" in Integrity & Maintenance next to Verify/Prune/Verify restorability (for domains whose off-site repo is marked append-only), with its last-checked state - previously it only existed as a button inside the off-site wizard, under the less obvious name "tamper test".
- **The tamper-test schedule says when it is inactive (#109).** If no off-site repo is marked append-only, that schedule never runs - the settings now show a clear "Inactive - …" note explaining why and how to enable it, instead of silently displaying a time that never fires.

## Fixed

- **The recovery kit now requires a login password.** The kit contains the master key and off-site credentials - everything needed to decrypt every backup, including the append-only off-site archives designed to survive a compromised server. It is no longer downloadable while no login password is set; set one under Settings → Security first.
- **"Back up all" for folder sets now batches its off-site replication** like the container batch and the scheduled runs do, instead of re-opening the off-site repo once per set.
- **No more scrollbars in the Protection status card (#98).** At narrow or half width the card now wraps each domain row into a clean stacked layout instead of showing a horizontal scrollbar under every row; at full width the aligned column grid is unchanged.
- **Sessions can now be revoked.** "Sign out everywhere" (Settings → Security) invalidates every issued login session; existing sessions survive the upgrade until you use it.
- **The metrics token is no longer echoed** by the settings API - it reports only whether one is stored, like every other secret.
- **Storage card rows no longer clip their sparkline** at half width, and the backup heatmap no longer duplicates a day when clocks fall back.
- **Missing translations filled in:** tamper-test results, the schedule toggles and two stray keys are now properly translated in all 26 languages (they showed English before).

- **Light mode is readable again (#105).** Status colours (the green/red/blue/yellow of chips, log lines, banners and badges) were hard-coded for the dark theme and nearly invisible on light backgrounds. All of them now switch with the theme: dark mode is pixel-identical to before, light mode uses proper high-contrast counterparts from the IBM Carbon light palette - including the backup heatmap, whose failure cells were the worst offender.

- **Log dates follow your region, not the UI language (#104).** The activity-log date was ordered by the app language, so an English UI showed US-style "07/24" even in Europe. It now follows your browser/system locale - Portugal sees "24/07" with the English UI - and searching by the displayed form or an ISO date keeps working.

- **Restore checks, tamper tests and the flash-ZIP export now show in the activity log WHILE they run (#109).** Scheduled restore checks could keep disks busy for a while with the log showing nothing until they finished. All three now publish a live line ("Restore check running - Containers …") that updates in place and hands over cleanly to the finished entry - same as backups and replication. They deliberately don't block the backup/restore buttons.
- **The log's date format can no longer disagree with the rest of the app (#108).** The activity log resolved its date locale differently from every other date in the UI, so on some systems (e.g. an English browser with a Portuguese region) only the log showed US-style dates. It now uses exactly the same system-default formatting as the rest of the app.

- **Tamper tests always show up in the activity log now (#109).** When the off-site repo is not a REST server (for example B2 or S3 object-lock immutability), the scheduled tamper test used to end without recording anything - the 08:00 schedule seemed to vanish. Every tamper run is now logged with an honest outcome: protected, FAILED, or skipped with the reason ("only REST repos are verifiable").
- **Off-site DR checks are distinguishable from local restore checks (#109).** Both used to log the identical "Restore check passed" line, so the DR proof was invisible in the log. The off-site DR drill now has its own entries - "Off-site DR check running …" live and "Off-site DR restore verified - Containers" when done - plus its own filter option.

- **Restore errors show the real cause (#110).** A failed restore reported only "Fatal: There were 1 errors" - restic emits the actual per-file errors in a JSON form the error extraction didn't understand, so the useful part was thrown away. The run entry, the activity log and the restore panel now carry the decoded causes (path-scrubbed, up to three plus a count), e.g. "restic restore failed: Fatal: There were 1 errors: open [path]: file exists". Applies to every restore path - folder restores, file picks, VM and DR restores.
- **Metadata-only restore warnings work again.** The case that downgrades a files restore to "success with warning" when only permission metadata could not be applied (issue #62) silently stopped matching when JSON progress was introduced - it now recognises both output forms.
- **The removed-container reminder is unambiguous now (#111).** "…is still a scheduled backup target" read like BombVault kept trying to back the container up. It now says plainly: nothing is backed up anymore, the existing backups are kept and restorable, and how to stop the reminder. It also only fires on the first skip (now pinned by tests), while the nightly skip entry stays in the log.

## Security & build hardening

- restic and rclone downloads are now checksum-verified against the official upstream hashes during the image build; a mismatch fails the build.
- All GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs and base images to digests; Renovate keeps the pins current.
